intro.heading: Aamchi Mumbai!
intro.lead: Devcon is where the people behind decentralized systems come together to learn, build, and connect, and this year it calls Mumbai home.
intro.body: Engineering talent runs deep in India, and its open-source community is expanding faster than almost any other in the world. Mumbai is where that energy and creative spirit gathers, and this November it's where Ethereum's does, too.

snapshot_values.water: Not universally potable. Use sealed bottles.

welcome.heading: Welcome to Mumbai
welcome.lead: Mumbai is one of India's largest cities and its financial capital, stretching along the Arabian Sea.
welcome.body_1: It's dense, energetic, and made up of distinct neighborhoods that feel very different from one another: historic colonial districts in the south, glossy business hubs in the center, and trendier residential areas along the western corridor.
welcome.body_2: It's a city of contrasts; glass towers sit alongside busy markets and street food stalls. The pace is fast, the streets are lively, and traffic can be intense.
welcome.zone_caption: Mumbai runs roughly north–south along the coast in distinct "micro-cities" that feel very different from one another.
welcome.devcon_lead: Devcon is coming to Mumbai to recognize and build on what India is already creating
welcome.devcon_body_1: India has one of the world's largest concentrations of engineering talent and one of its fastest-growing open-source communities.
welcome.devcon_body_2: Infrastructure, ZK identity systems, and coordination layers built in India already power Ethereum globally, including India's established ecosystem of communities like [ETHMumbai](https://www.ethmumbai.in/), [Devfolio](https://devfolio.co/), and [Polygon](https://polygon.technology/) (founded in Mumbai as Matic Network).
welcome.video_quote: "It will be the whole world, all of Ethereum coming over to Mumbai, and being able to see the spirit of Ethereum right there."

getting_there.heading: Getting to Mumbai
getting_there.lead: BKC (Bandra Kurla Complex) is Mumbai's modern corporate district, easily accessible from the airport.
getting_there.body: Devcon will take place at the Jio World Centre, a large convention venue in Mumbai's BKC district.

air.title: Arriving by air
air.body:
Mumbai is served by **[Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (BOM)](https://csmia.adaniairports.com/)**, the city's primary airport.

- **Terminal 2 (T2):** Most international flights and several domestic airlines
- **Terminal 1 (T1):** Select domestic flights

The terminals are in different locations, so double-check your arrival terminal before traveling.
air.image_alt: Inside Terminal 2 of Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport

options.title: App-based cabs
options.body: Uber, Ola and Rapido are widely available. Follow the airport signs to the designated app-cab pickup area near the arrivals exit.

options.title: Prepaid taxis
options.body: Official prepaid taxi counters are located inside the airport and are a useful alternative if you don't have mobile data or an Indian number.

options.title: Mumbai Metro
options.body: The metro is another convenient option for traveling from the airport towards BKC, South Mumbai and other parts of the city.

train.title: Arriving by train
train.body:
Mumbai's main long-distance railway terminals include:

- Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus — **CSMT**
- Mumbai Central — **MMCT**
- Bandra Terminus — **BDTS**
- Lokmanya Tilak Terminus — **LTT**
- Dadar — **DDR/DR**

Check the exact station listed on your ticket, as these terminals are located in different parts of the city.

**Metro access:** BKC station on Metro Line 3 is located between 200m and 1.3 km from the Jio venue entrance.
train.image_alt: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus seen through a stone archway

car.title: Arriving by car
car.body: Parking is available in the BKC basement car parking facility and includes charging stations for electric vehicles.
car.image_alt: The BKC basement car parking facility

getting_there.tips:
- Download **Uber**, **Ola** and **Google Maps** before arriving.
- Save your hotel and venue address offline.
- Allow extra travel time during rush hours and heavy rain.
- Avoid unsolicited taxi offers inside or outside the terminal.
- Black-and-yellow taxis are metered, but app cabs are easier for first-timers.
- Auto-rickshaws operate mainly in the suburbs, not South Mumbai.
getting_there.booth_body_1: If you are arriving at Mumbai Airport Terminal 2, look out for the Devcon Welcome Booth in the arrivals area, shortly after baggage collection.
getting_there.booth_body_2: Our team will be there to welcome attendees, help with basic arrival questions, and share useful information for getting around Mumbai and reaching your accommodation.
getting_there.banner: Look out for the **Devcon Welcome Booth** at arrivals in Mumbai Airport **Terminal 2**

stay.heading: Where to stay
stay.lead: Pick where you stay by the commute to Jio World Centre, not just by neighborhood.
stay.body: A 3km trip in Mumbai can take 10 minutes at dawn or 45 minutes at 6pm. Devcon overlaps with **[Diwali](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Diwali-Hindu-festival)**, India's biggest festival, so book your stay early as rooms will go fast.
stay.aside: We'd generally recommend established hotel chains, though Airbnb and independent hotels work fine too. Unsure about a specific place? Ask in the Devcon [Telegram group](https://t.me/+sitvvHw8D8EzN2Yx).

hotels.name: Tripsha
hotels.body: Discounted rooms and perks for Devcon attendees. Rooms are subject to availability on a first come, first served basis.

hotels.name: FLYFI.IO
hotels.body: Flyfi is a wallet-native hotel booking platform for Web3. Book 300,000+ hotels worldwide, pay with crypto, and travel without creating an account. No weird retargeting ads, no data trail.

hotels.name: Niranta Transit Hotel
hotels.body: Directly connected to Terminal 2 of Mumbai airport. An accessible option if your flight lands late, or you need a buffer before traveling to or from the city.

stay.more_hotels_body:
- **Indie Stays** (BKC Kalina) sits about 3km from JWCC, though traffic can stretch that to 15–25 minutes.
- **ibis Mumbai BKC** is the strongest pick if you want consistency with a business-hotel feel, restaurant, and workspaces; rooms are compact but reliable.
- **T24 Retro** (Vile Parle East) is a stylish boutique option with easy access to BKC, good for once Indie Stays or ibis price out.
- **Hotel Bawa International**, also in Vile Parle East, is a straightforward business stay convenient for both the airport and BKC.

areas.title: South Mumbai (SoBo)
areas.body:
- **Colaba:** Visitor-friendly, Gateway of India, cafés, galleries
- **Fort / Kala Ghoda:** Colonial architecture, museums, heritage feel
- **Marine Drive / Churchgate:** Seafront promenade, Art Deco, great sunsets
- **Nariman Point:** Corporate, polished
- **Malabar Hill:** Leafy, upscale, residential
- **Girgaon / Charni Road:** Traditional, local markets, near Chowpatty Beach
- **Byculla:** Everyday Mumbai, museums
- **Worli:** High-rises plus fishing-village roots (Worli Koliwada)

areas.title: Bandra & Western Corridor
areas.body:
- **Bandra West:** Social center, cafés, bars, street art
- **Khar:** Quieter Bandra, upscale dining
- **Santacruz:** West calmer/upmarket, East more utilitarian
- **Juhu:** Beachfront, relaxed, affluent
- **Bandra East:** Commercial, direct BKC connection

areas.title: Central Mumbai
areas.body:
- **Lower Parel:** Malls, offices, restaurants, nightlife hub
- **Prabhadevi:** Residential, Siddhivinayak Temple
- **Dadar:** Major transit node, intense local markets
- **Matunga:** South Indian character, calm, good food

areas.title: Andheri
areas.body:
- **Andheri West:** Food, nightlife, media energy; Lokhandwala dining/shopping
- **Andheri East:** Office parks, metro access, airport proximity

stay.avoid_body:
- Dharavi (at night)
- Kamathipura
- Falkland Road

Learn more in the [Safety section](#safety)

safety.heading: Safety
safety.lead: Generally, major national travel advisories recommend exercising increased or a higher degree of caution in India.
safety.body_1: Importantly, Mumbai is not currently identified by any of the advisories cited below as a "do not travel," "avoid all travel", or equivalent destination; it instead falls within broader India-wide advice.
safety.body_2: Taken together, the advisories state that terrorism remains a risk and that attacks may affect public places, including places visited by tourists and foreign nationals. They note that serious crime against foreign travellers is less frequent, but incidents of violent crime and sexual assault do occur. They also warn that women travellers may experience unwanted attention, harassment or sexual assault; that petty theft, scams and drink spiking occur; and that demonstrations and large gatherings can sometimes become violent or dangerous.
safety.body_3: The advisories generally recommend staying aware of your surroundings, taking care of personal belongings and unattended food or drinks, avoiding demonstrations, monitoring local developments, and following instructions from local authorities. Stronger warnings apply to certain specified regions outside Mumbai.
safety.body_4: Travelers should check their own government's latest advisory before and during travel, as official guidance can change.

gender.title: Gender-based safety & LGBTQ+ safety
gender.body_1: Official national travel advisories cited below do not currently advise women travelers against traveling to Mumbai.
gender.body_2: Generally, as part of their broader guidance for India, they note that women travelers may encounter unwanted attention or harassment and that sexual assaults have been reported, including in cities and tourist areas. The advisories provide practical precautions, particularly for women traveling alone, such as taking additional care at night or in quiet or unlit places, being careful when using public transport or taxis, and keeping food and drinks attended. Stronger travel warnings apply to specified regions elsewhere in India.
gender.body_3: Mumbai's suburban trains have [women-only compartments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women-only_passenger_car#India), and it's best to avoid local trains at peak hours (roughly 8–10am and 5–8pm). It's recommended to use Uber/Ola after dark.
gender.body_4: Same-sex relationships have been legal in India since 2018, but same-sex marriage is [not legally recognized](https://outrightinternational.org/our-work/asia/india). India [legally recognizes](https://translaw.clpr.org.in/case-law/nalsa-third-gender-identity/) a third gender. Mumbai has one of the [country's most visible and active](https://humsafar.org/about-us/) queer communities, and India is [generally considered safe](https://www.worldnomads.com/travel-safety/southern-asia/india/is-india-safe-for-lgbt-travelers) for LGBTQ+ travelers.

air.title: Air quality & masks
air.body:
November–February is historically [Mumbai's worst window for air quality](https://www.iqair.com/air-quality/india/maharashtra/mumbai) because the dry season removes the rain that normally clears the air. This doesn't mean venue days will be unsafe, but it's recommended to **pack a basic N95-style mask** and use it if it makes you more comfortable.

You likely won't need a mask constantly, as most of your time at the Devcon event will be indoors at the venue or in hotels/cafés. But outdoor time in BKC and heavy-traffic corridors is worth masking up for if you're at all sensitive to air quality.

Outdoor mask use is [particularly recommended](https://sahyadrihospital.com/blog/how-can-i-protect-my-lungs-from-diwali-firecracker-smoke/) if you're extending your stay for the Diwali festival, when firework smoke adds to the load for a few days afterward.

food.title: Food, water & restaurants near the venue
food.body_1:
The [CDC advises travelers](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/asia/india.html) to India not to drink tap water and to use only [sealed, factory-bottled water](https://cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/preparing-international-travelers/food-and-water-precautions-for-travelers.html), including for brushing your teeth.

Major bottled water brands like Bisleri, Aquafina, and Kinley are easily available at most places in Mumbai. It is also [recommended to avoid ice](https://cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/preparing-international-travelers/food-and-water-precautions-for-travelers.html) unless you're confident it's made from purified water.

For street food, follow the CDC guidance that [fully cooked food served hot is safest](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/asia/india.html); ease into street food via high-turnover stalls where it's cooked in front of you (don't miss trying foods like vada pav, pav bhaji, bhel puri, thali, and coastal Konkani seafood).

around.title: Getting around safely
around.body_1:
**App-based cabs** are the easiest way for first-time visitors to get around. **Uber**, **Ola**, and **Rapido** all operate across Mumbai, with fixed upfront pricing and trip tracking you can share with a friend.

Mumbai's black-and-yellow taxis are metered and generally reliable, but [avoid unsolicited taxi or guide offers in tourist areas](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/india/safety-and-security), where scams targeting foreigners [are common](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/asia/india). At the airport, use the designated app-cab pickup zones or the official prepaid taxi counters inside the terminal. Auto-rickshaws operate in the suburbs (including around BKC) but aren't permitted in South Mumbai.
around.body_2:
For the venue, Metro Line 3 is the fastest and most comfortable option, reaching BKC from the airport in around 5 minutes. If you try the suburban local trains, [travel outside rush hour](https://realitytoursandtravel.com/guide-mumbai-trains/) and keep bags in front of you in crowds, where [pickpocketing is the main risk](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/india/safety-and-security).

After dark, book an app cab rather than walking or hailing on the street, and follow the [standard advisory guidance](https://travel.state.gov/en/international-travel/travel-advisories/india.html) to stick to well-known venues and avoid isolated areas, avoiding dimly-lit bylanes anywhere in the city, and isolated spots after 10pm.

notes: Use your **right hand** when paying or handing items
**Bargain at markets**, not at fixed-price shops
A head wobble means **yes**, not no

wear.title: General
wear.body: Light, breathable fabrics and comfortable walking shoes. Early November is warm (30–32°C daytime) even though it's the "cooler" season.

wear.title: Temples and religious sites
wear.body: Dress modestly, with shoulders and knees covered. It's worth packing one modest outfit even if the rest of your wardrobe is conference-casual.

wear.title: At the venue
wear.body: Jio World Centre's air conditioning can get cold. Bring a light jacket to transition from hot outdoor spaces to cooler inside events.

culture.diwali_1: **[Diwali](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Diwali-Hindu-festival)**, the festival of lights, falls on November 8, two days after Devcon ends.
culture.diwali_2: It's the one festival nearly the whole country celebrates together: homes glow with oil lamps, doorsteps fill with rangoli patterns, and fireworks light up the evenings. If you're extending your stay, it's a rare chance to experience India at its most festive.
culture.diwali_3: Book accommodation early, since rooms fill fast around the holiday, and see the air quality notes in the Safety section if fireworks smoke is a concern for you.
culture.bollywood_1: **[Bollywood](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Bollywood-film-industry-India)** is woven into everyday life in Mumbai, the industry's home city, and watching a film in a local theater is an experience in itself.
culture.bollywood_2: The timing is good: Ramayana Part 1, one of the year's biggest releases, a big-screen epic based on the Ramayana with music by Hans Zimmer, opens in theaters on November 5, during Devcon week.
culture.bollywood_3: Tickets for this and everything else are on [BookMyShow](https://in.bookmyshow.com/). For a crash course before you land, locals recommend starting with Swades, Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani, or Zindagi Na Milegi Doobara.
culture.video_caption: shares a few must-do's when visiting India: from testing your spice tolerance to exploring historic temples.

payments.heading: Payments & Crypto in India
payments.cards_lead: Visa/Mastercard are widely accepted; Amex is less reliable outside luxury hotels.
payments.cards_body: Cash is still useful for autos, street food, and small shops. ATMs brands include HDFC, ICICI, SBI, and Kotak.
payments.upi_body:
UPI is a mobile-based payment system developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). Visitors will notice UPI payment QR codes everywhere in Mumbai, from restaurants to street stalls. Here's how it works for foreign visitors:

1. Pick a UPI One World partner app. [CheQ](https://www.chequpi.com/) and [Mony](https://havemony.com/) are built specifically for foreign travelers, or IDFC First Bank's app.
2. Complete KYC with passport + visa, either in person at an airport kiosk (Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru all have these in international arrivals), or digitally through the app itself (CheQ and Mony both support digital KYC; Mony provides post-arrival verification within 24-48 hours via an agent).
3. Load the wallet with an international card or cash.
4. Scan any UPI QR code and pay with a PIN. UPI works at everything from street food stalls to five-star hotels.
5. Any unused balance can be refunded back to your original card before you leave. Don't skip this step, it has to be done before departure, not after.

Typical wallet limits (~INR 2,00,000/month) are well above what a Devcon trip will need. There are no onboarding or transaction fees to use UPI.
payments.digital_1: India has introduced specific anti-money laundering and tax requirements applicable to certain digital assets and related transactions, as defined under Indian law.
payments.digital_2: India's legal and regulatory landscape in relation to digital assets and related transactions continues to evolve. If you intend to engage in activities involving digital assets while in India (for example, buying, selling, trading, payments, or token-related transactions), please ensure you understand the applicable legal and tax requirements before doing so and, where appropriate, seek advice from qualified legal and tax professionals familiar with Indian law.

events.heading: Side events & Community
events.lead: Devcon week is bigger than the venue: expect meetups, hackathons, and community gatherings across Mumbai in the days around the conference, hosted by local and global Ethereum communities alike.
events.body_1: The gathering has already started. **Road to Devcon** is a year of community-run events across India, from Mumbai and Bengaluru to Kerala and Jaipur, building toward Devcon 8.
events.body_2: Browse upcoming events, meet the communities behind them, or get your own event listed.
